item.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.30314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $\theta$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $\theta$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+\theta(r)+\theta^2(r)$ but need not commute with $\theta$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,\theta;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Deep H. Makadiya

item.title: On a finite group in which every non-nilpotent maximal invariant subgroup of order divisible by $p$ is normal
item.description: arXiv:2610.30653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ and $G$ be finite groups such that $A$ acts coprimely on $G$ by automorphisms. For any fixed prime divisor $p$ of $|G|$, we prove that if every non-nilpotent maximal $A$-invariant subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ is normal then $G$ has a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li, Na Li

item.title: On the generation of the symmetric group by index relations of three prefix reversals
item.description: arXiv:2610.30892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The cubic pancake graphs are Cayley graphs over the symmetric group Sn generated by three prefix reversals. There is the folllowing open problem: characterize all the sets of three prefix reversals that generate Sn. Blanco and Golubyatnikov give a complete solution of the problem when any of the two smallest or the two largest lengths but n are included in a triple of prefix reversals. According to their conjectures, we give some conditions implying a triple of prefix reversals does not generate Sn. Moreover, Using the symmetric groups that can already be generated by three prefix reversals, we can derive some recurrence conditions.
item.dc:creator: Yexiao Lei, Jinxing Zhao, Ziyu Zhu, Yang Wu

item.title: Orbits of $p$-Nilpotent Group Actions for Small Primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.30952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite solvable group and $V$ be a faithful completely reducible $G$-module. We improve previous bounds for the sizes of defect groups of blocks of solvable groups through an improved bound on vector stabilizers of $p$-nilpotent groups. Specifically, if $G$ is 2-nilpotent and $2 \nmid |V|$, then there exists $v \in V$ such that $\mathbf{C}_G(v) \leq \mathbf{F}_4(G)$. Similarly, if $G$ is 3-nilpotent and $3 \nmid |V|$, then there exists $v \in V$ such that $\mathbf{C}_G(v) \leq \mathbf{F}_5(G)$. Using these results, we conclude that $d(B) \leq \lfloor \frac{9n}{10} \rfloor$ when $O_p(G) = 1$ for $p = 2$ and $d(B) \leq \lfloor \frac{19n}{21} \rfloor$ when $O_p(G) = 1$ for $p = 3$.
item.dc:creator: Chloe So, Yong Yang

item.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
item.description: arXiv:2610.31535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < \pi/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $\pi/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Larotonda

item.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
item.description: arXiv:2610.31379v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $\Gamma\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $\Gamma$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Verjovsky

item.title: Searching for the power rangers
item.description: arXiv:2610.31548v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup). This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.
item.dc:creator: Rapha\"el Carroy, Julien Melleray

item.title: Groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers are complete co-analytic
item.description: arXiv:2610.31601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that the set of groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is a complete co-analytic subset of the Polish space of countable groups. This answers a question of Wesolek and Williams.
item.dc:creator: Hakk{\i} Ka\u{g}an Yumak

item.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
item.description: arXiv:2610.31602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.
item.dc:creator: Mikey Becht, Darij Grinberg

item.title: Random Burnside Groups
item.description: arXiv:1705.08060v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fix integers $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$. For every sufficiently large fixed odd exponent $M$, choose $k$ independent elements uniformly from the sphere of radius $\ell$ in the free Burnside group $B_m(M)$. We prove that the quotient by their normal closure is infinite with probability at least $1-e^{-c\ell}$. More precisely, the quotient map has no nontrivial kernel element of length at most $\kappa\ell$, for constants $c,\kappa>0$. We also consider the analogue of the Gromov positive density model for the Burnside variety.
item.dc:creator: O. Kharlampovich, A. Miasnikov

item.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
item.description: arXiv:2411.00739v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $r>2$, and let $\Gamma_{2r} \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}) \ast (\mathbb{Z}/2r\mathbb{Z})$ be the Hecke group. Let $\mathcal{N}_\ell$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements with cyclically reduced word length exactly $\ell$ in the standard generating set of $\Gamma_{2r}$. Let $P(x)$ be the polynomial \[ P(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{i=1}^{r-1} x^{i} - 1. \] Let $\rho$ be the unique positive root of $P$ and $C$ be a constant depending on $r.$ We prove that, as $\ell \to \infty$, \[|\mathcal{N}_\ell| \sim C\rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{\ell+1}{2} \right\rfloor}. \] Our approach exploits the free product structure of $\Gamma_{2r}$, together with a combinatorial counting function and recurrence relations arising from cyclically reduced representatives. We further show that the asymptotic growth rate of primitive reciprocal conjugacy classes of word length $\ell$ coincides with that of $\mathcal{N}_\ell$. This result extends previous work for odd values of $p$ and provides a uniform asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.
item.dc:creator: Debattam Das, Krishnendu Gongopadhyay

item.title: Representations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and hyperplane complements
item.description: arXiv:2511.04836v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study faithful realisations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and study Vinberg systems associated to them. We show that they induce embeddings of hyperplane complements, which provide geometrical realisations of certain types of strong admissible (LCM) homomorphisms between Artin--Tits groups.
item.dc:creator: Edmund Heng, Luis Paris

item.title: Weak rank rigidity for groups with a navigable path system
item.description: arXiv:2605.29837v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that groups with a mild form of non-positive curvature (a navigable path system) satisfy the weak rank rigidity conjecture: they either have linear divergence or a Morse element. This class includes discrete groups of projective automorphisms of open convex cones, Helly groups (answering a question of Genevois), Coxeter groups, weak Garside groups (in particular Deligne's groups and fundamental groups of Salvetti complexes of oriented matroids), hierarchically hyperbolic groups, and other examples. Along the way, we show that those groups satisfy the Morse local-to-global property, providing a unified proof for the whole class. In the metric setting, the same condition of non-positive curvature allows to provide a local definition (that is, in a sense, optimal) of rank one/Morse geodesics, mirroring the one using parallel Jacobi fields from Riemannian geometry; to deduce linearity of divergence from linearity on a sequence; to obtain new cases in which Morse geodesics are strongly contracting. The main new tool introduced is the generalised contraction space, a hyperbolic space that encodes the negative curvature of a given space.
item.dc:creator: Cornelia Drutu, Davide Spriano, Stefanie Zbinden

item.title: The Weyl-orbit embedding and a representation-theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy
item.description: arXiv:2606.16862v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Bu, Gu, and Jaffe introduced the quantum uniformity measures to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. We prove that the quantum uniformity measures are the pullbacks of the matrix-valued uniformity functionals of Gowers and Hatami under the map $U\mapsto(a\mapsto W_aUW_a^*)$, which we call the Weyl-orbit embedding. We study the structure of the Weyl-orbit embedding, and among other results, establish a canonical decomposition of the ambient matrix-valued uniformity space into uniformity preserving twisted copies of the quantum uniformity space. The Weyl-orbit embedding identifies the Clifford hierarchy with Leibman polynomial maps. This identification yields a representation theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy in terms of unitary representations of the universal polynomial groups introduced by the first author and Thom.
item.dc:creator: Asgar Jamneshan, Berke \"Unal

item.title: On weak commutativity between $n$ isomorphic groups, $n \geq 2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.07330v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Weak Commutativity Group was defined by the first author in the early 1980's as $ \chi(H) = \langle H, H^\psi \mid [h,h^\psi] = 1, \ \forall h \in H \rangle $ where $H$ and $H^\psi$ are isomorphic groups under an isomorphism $\psi$, and proved that $\chi(-)$, seen as a group operator, preserved the classes of solvable groups, finite groups, finite $p$-groups, and perfect groups. The list has grown considerably since then (see references). It is clear that the iterated operator $\chi^n (-)$ also preserves the same classes. However, we observe that for $n \geq 2$ many of the $2^n$ $H$-generating copies of $\chi^n (H)$ fail to weakly commute among themselves. We introduce in this paper the "$n$-ary Weak Commutativity Group" generated by $n$ copies of $H$ which weakly commute among themselves; that is $ \chi_n (H) = \langle H, H^\psi, \dots, H^{\psi_{n-1}} \mid [h^{\psi_i}, h^{\psi_j}] = 1, \ \forall h \in H, \ 0 \leq i < j \leq n-1 \rangle $ (by definition, $H^{\psi_0} = H, H^{\psi_1} = H^\psi$). We study quotients of $\chi^n (H)$ which are also simultaneously quotients of $\chi_{2^n} (H)$; we refer to them as Hybrid $\chi^n (H)$ - $\chi_{2^n} (H)$ groups. For $n=2$ we determine the largest common quotient $Q(H)$ of $\chi^2(H)$ and $\chi_4(H)$, that is, the largest hybrid $\chi^2(H)$-$\chi_4(H)$ group. A related class of groups in our study is $\chi(n,H)$, a quotient of $\chi_n(H)$, previously introduced by the third named author in his 2007 doctoral thesis. We prove that this class of groups continues to preserve finiteness, nilpotency and perfectness, and we provide detailed information about their structure. In contrast, $\chi_n(H)$ behaves differently: $\chi_3(C_2 \times C_2)$ is infinite, while $\chi_3(C_{p^t} \times C_{p^u})$ is finite for $p$ odd.
item.dc:creator: Said N. Sidki, Nora\'i R. Rocco, Ricardo N. de Oliveira, Dmytro Savchuk

item.title: A simultaneous variant of the Hall-Paige theorem and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.21600v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $k\geq 1$ , we say that a finite group $G$ satisfies property $\mathcal P_k$ if, for every $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_k\in\operatorname{Aut}(G)$, there exists a bijection $f$ of $G$ such that each map $g\mapsto \beta_i(g)f(g)$ is a bijection. For $k=1$ this is equivalent to the classical Hall--Paige complete mapping property. We prove that if $p$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, then $G$ satisfies $\mathcal P_k$ for every $k<p-1$ and we show that this bound is sharp. For finite abelian $p$-groups, the bijection $f$ may moreover be chosen to be an automorphism, and for noncyclic homocyclic $p$-groups this remains true for $k=p-1$. Finally, we interpret $\mathcal P_k$ in terms of common transversals and common orthogonal mates of Latin squares generated from automorphisms and the Cayley table of a finite group $G$.
item.dc:creator: Maria Loukaki

item.title: Classification of finite subgroups of generalized cactus groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the finite groups that embed into generalized cactus groups associated with arbitrary Coxeter systems. Every finite subgroup is conjugate to a subgroup of the generalized cactus group associated with a finite standard parabolic subgroup of the underlying Coxeter group. This reduces the classification to explicit lists of finite groups for the finite irreducible Coxeter systems. For types B, D, E, F, and H, we analyze cube stabilizers to obtain these lists. For type $I_2(p)$, we determine the associated generalized cactus group directly from its defining presentation. We explicitly realize every listed group as a subgroup of the corresponding generalized cactus group. When the Coxeter diagram has finitely many vertices, we determine the largest order and all possible orders of finite subgroups. In type A, we prove directly that a finite group embeds into the ordinary cactus group on $n$ strands if and only if it embeds into a Sylow 2-subgroup of the symmetric group on $n$ letters. We also give weighted embedding criteria in types A and B and counterexamples to Genevois's conjecture on finite subgroups of cactus groups.
item.dc:creator: Junseok Kim

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang, Jimmie Lawson
